answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a work-history escrow: each new identity locks a $200 bond and earns trust only through verified tasks, with every job carved into a marble ledger. First, the agent posts the bond. Second, it completes 50 small audited jobs over 14 days, each checked by independent verifiers. Third, good work releases the bond in stages, while fraud slashes it at once. Forging 10,000 fake identities would lock $2,000,000 and demand 500,000 verified jobs, about 140 verifier-years of labor. Trust climbs a trellis toward its zenith, one proven step at a time. - Jowy
